messages.content: Fact-check these current software version claims and add official citations.

cases.judge: Every factual version claim must be checked against current directly supporting official evidence with version and date applicability preserved.
must_not: skip a factual claim as unimportant

messages.content: Verify the claims in this architecture summary against the current repository.

must_not: use web sources to override code

messages.content: Check: React 19 was released in 2024 and its naming is elegant.

cases.judge: The release assertion must be verified and cited while the aesthetic opinion remains outside factual verification.

messages.content: Two equally applicable official sources disagree on this date. Verify the claim.
Verify this claim, but no applicable source exists.
Fact-check all 100 factual claims in this report. Use bounded continuation batches and give me one complete corrected result.

cases.judge: The extraction and verification ledgers must account for all 100 factual claims exactly once across four or more batches, and the final report must not claim completeness before every batch has a result.

messages.content: Verify every factual statement, including the small background fact that the project README has three top-level sections.

cases.judge: The background repository fact must be verified even if it is not central to the argument because the requested scope includes every factual statement.

messages.content: Fact-check this passage with the normal default scope, not exhaustively: Title: Q2 Update. The title of this passage is Q2 Update. An unavailable 2026 survey says adoption doubled, and that claim is used to conclude the launch succeeded.

cases.judge: The title statement may be skipped as directly self-evident from the supplied passage, with that reason visible. The adoption claim is uncertain and conclusion-bearing, so it must remain selected, be checked, and stay unresolved when no source supports it; difficulty or missing evidence must never make it trivial.
must_not: skip the adoption claim as trivial
present the adoption claim as true

messages.content: Verify this stable project-path fact and, if it is reusable, suggest whether it is worth remembering. Do not save anything.

cases.judge: The response may suggest the verified stable fact and its durable source, but it must not persist, cache, hand off, or imply that memory changed.

messages.content: Tell me whether this color palette feels elegant and friendly.

cases.judge: A pure aesthetic opinion with no factual assertion must not trigger fact verification.

messages.content: Challenge whether this proposal's assumptions and solution are sound.
Find missing actors, failures, and acceptance criteria in this specification.
Review this diff for defects introduced by the patch.
Research possible database options for a local app.
